title: E. Product of Closures
statement:
Let the closure of a positive integer $$x  \gt  0$$ be the following infinite binary string $$C(x)$$:

For example, $$C(1)$$ $$=$$ 11111... , $$C(4)$$ $$=$$ 10010010010010... , $$C(9)$$ $$=$$ 100110011001... .

Let the product of two closures $$C(x) \mathop{\&} C(y)$$ be the infinite binary string obtained by the bitwise binary AND of the strings $$C(x)$$ and $$C(y)$$. For example, for $$C(4) \mathop{\&} C(9)$$ we get

$$$ \begin{array}{r} \begin{array}{r} C(4)\\ C(9)\\ \end{array} \mathop{\&} \begin{array}{r} 100100100100100100...\\ 100110011001100110...\\ \end{array} \\ \hline \begin{array}{r} 100100000000100100... \end{array} \end{array} $$$

You are given three integers $$l$$, $$r$$, and $$n$$. Among all numbers in the segment $$[l, r]$$, find two integers $$x$$ and $$y$$ ($$l $\leq x  \lt  y \leq r$$$) such that $$C(x) \mathop{\&} C(y)$$ is lexicographically smallest , and print the first $$n$$ binary symbols of this product.

The first line contains one integer $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 1000$$$) — the number of test cases.

The only line of each test case contains three integers $$l$$, $$r$$, and $$n$$ ($$1 $\leq l  \lt  r  \lt  2^{30}$$$; $$1 $\leq n \leq 1000$$$) — the range of possible values and the length of the answer.

For each test case, print one binary string of length $$n$$ — the first $$n$$ symbols of the lexicographically smallest product of closures.

In the first test case, the lexicographically smallest string is obtained by the product $$C(2) \mathop{\&} C(4)$$.
input: Input The first line contains one integer $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 1000$$$) — the number of test cases. The only line of each test case contains three integers $$l$$, $$r$$, and $$n$$ ($$1 $\leq l  \lt  r  \lt  2^{30}$$$; $$1 $\leq n \leq 1000$$$) — the range of possible values and the length of the answer.
output: Output For each test case, print one binary string of length $$n$$ — the first $$n$$ symbols of the lexicographically smallest product of closures.
